bootstrap.notes: No ml/ or docs/ directory existed before this stage. First stage of a new pipeline on the existing dhaka_kacchi_ai_harness warehouse.

decisions.decision: task_type = binary_classification (above/below platform-relative typical engagement), not regression on raw likes/comments/shares/reach.
decisions.rationale: With ~140 posts per platform and metrics on incompatible scales across platforms (Threads views vs Facebook impressions vs Instagram reach), a precise regression invites false precision on too little data. A relative tier is robust and still decision-useful.

decisions.decision: Label = 1 if a post's likes+comments+shares exceeds the EXPANDING median of that same platform's posts up to that point in time; else 0.
decisions.rationale: Using the whole-dataset (including future) median to define 'typical' would leak backward — a post published in month 1 would be judged against posts published in month 6. An expanding, platform-specific median avoids that while staying simple.

decisions.decision: Threads posts are excluded from the primary binary label and initial model scope; Facebook (and Instagram, pending re-ingest) are the primary platforms.
decisions.rationale: Live query against the local warehouse (2026-09-23) showed 56 of 57 real Threads posts have likes+comments+shares = 0 (Facebook: 161/228 posts have nonzero engagement). A platform-median split on Threads would put ~98% of posts in one class, which is a degenerate label, not a usable one. Threads' one real engagement signal is `views`, a fundamentally different metric than the like/comment/share signal the other platforms share — folding it into the same label without adjustment would be a modeling error I can name in advance rather than discover after training.
alternatives_considered: include Threads with the same label definition (rejected: near-zero variance, discovered via live query)
define a Threads-specific label on `views` instead (deferred: revisit once Instagram data closes the more urgent gap; Threads is also only 57 posts)

decisions.decision: Initial feature set is pre-publish tabular/text only: platform, content_type, caption text, day-of-week, hour. No raw video/image pixel features in this pass.
decisions.rationale: User asked whether transfer learning fits and whether raw video should be an input. With ~350-480 total posts, fine-tuning any vision/video model from scratch is data-starved. The realistic use of transfer learning here is a frozen pretrained embedding (caption text embedding, or a pretrained image encoder on a thumbnail) added as a FEATURE later, not full retraining — deferred to 01-data/03-modeling once the tabular baseline exists and can show whether such a feature is even worth the added complexity.

decisions.decision: Floor = balanced accuracy >= 0.60 on the primary metric, set before any model has been run.
decisions.rationale: Genuinely uncertain whether ~350-480 rows of caption/content_type/timing data carries enough signal to clear even a modest bar over the 0.50 dummy. Set low enough to be achievable if there's any real signal, high enough that a model matching the dummy still fails it.

assertions.claim: Facebook engagement (likes+comments+shares) has enough variance for a non-degenerate median split.
assertions.method: Live SQL query against local warehouse: count of posts with engagement > 0 vs = 0, per platform, plus avg/median/min/max engagement per platform.
assertions.evidence: facebook: n=228, avg=3.19, median=2.0, range 0-45, 161/228 posts nonzero. threads: n=57, avg=0.018, median=0.0, range 0-1, only 1/57 posts nonzero.

assertions.claim: Threads engagement supports the same label definition as Facebook.
assertions.method: Same live SQL query as above, evaluated specifically for the threads platform.
assertions.evidence: 56 of 57 Threads posts have likes+comments+shares = 0; a median split would yield a ~2% positive rate. Threads excluded from the primary label as a result (see decision threads-excluded-from-primary-label).

assertions.claim: The floor (balanced accuracy >= 0.60) was set before any model was trained.
assertions.method: No model code exists yet in this repo; ml/ directory created for the first time in this stage.

assertions.claim: The dummy baseline (coin-flip / most-frequent-class) is not degenerate on the primary metric.
assertions.method: Label is constructed to be ~50/50 by definition (median split), so most-frequent-class and coin-flip dummies coincide and balanced accuracy for either is ~0.50, not a flattering 0/1 extreme.

assertions.claim: Prediction time (immediately before publishing, after caption/media/timing are decided) is specific enough to audit a candidate feature against.
assertions.method: Manual review of the feature list against warehouse schema: platform, content_type, caption text, day-of-week, hour are all knowable pre-publish; likes/comments/shares/reach/impressions/views are all post-hoc and explicitly excluded as features.

assertions.claim: Instagram posts (132, per DATA_CONSTRAINTS.md's real production ingest) are available in the local warehouse used for this ML work.
assertions.method: Live SQL query: `select platform, count(*) from social_post group by platform` against local DATABASE_URL. Initially failed (0 instagram rows), so `warehouse.ingest.instagram` was re-run locally in this same session and the query repeated.
assertions.evidence: Re-ingest landed 132 raw rows / upserted 132 posts / 132 snapshots, exit code 0, matching production's documented 132 exactly. Local corpus is now facebook=228, instagram=132, threads=57 (417 total, threads excluded from the primary label per decision threads-excluded-from-primary-label).

risks.description: Total corpus is ~350 (Facebook + Threads, local) to ~480 (once Instagram is re-ingested locally) posts, and the primary-platform corpus for this label (Facebook + Instagram) is smaller still. Statistical power for detecting a real effect is limited.
risks.mitigation: Stopping condition explicitly allows and expects a negative finding rather than indefinite tuning; floor set modestly (0.60) for the same reason.

risks.description: Threads' real engagement (likes/comments/shares) is near-zero across nearly every post; its only substantive metric is `views`, which is not comparable to the like/comment/share signal used for Facebook/Instagram.
risks.mitigation: Threads excluded from the primary model in this pass. Revisit with a Threads-specific label on `views` only if/when Threads' post volume grows enough to be worth a separate model.

risks.description: At the start of this stage, Instagram had zero rows in the local warehouse despite being real, ingested data in production.
risks.mitigation: Resolved within this stage: re-ran `warehouse.ingest.instagram` locally, landed all 132 posts, confirmed via live query. No longer an open gap, kept here for the record.

risks.description: Caption text as a raw feature (vs. simple derived stats like length/hashtag count) may need real NLP preprocessing (embeddings, TF-IDF) that hasn't been scoped yet.
risks.mitigation: 01-data/03-modeling to decide feature representation once EDA on captions is done; starting with simple derived stats (length, hashtag count, emoji count) is the safe default.

outputs.name: Problem framing doc
outputs.description: Copy for the repo's own docs, committed alongside the code.

next_stage_needs: Confirm Instagram row count in local warehouse before EDA (target: 132 rows, matching production per DATA_CONSTRAINTS.md).
Run the modality screen: this is tabular + short text (caption), not image/video pixels in this pass — expect route=classical_first unless EDA finds otherwise.
Compute the expanding per-platform median label defined here on the real Facebook + Instagram corpus and report the resulting class balance before splitting.

problem_spec.decision: Before publishing a drafted organic social post (Instagram/Facebook), flag whether it is likely to underperform that platform's own typical engagement, so the operator can revise caption/media/timing or post anyway knowing the odds.
problem_spec.actor: Dhaka Kacchi's sole operator, reviewing a drafted post before hitting publish.
problem_spec.target_definition: 1 if a post's (likes + comments + shares) exceeds the expanding median of that same platform's posts up to and including that post's posted_at timestamp; 0 otherwise. Computed only for Facebook and Instagram in this pass (see decision threads-excluded-from-primary-label). Uses only past posts to define 'typical' at each point in time, never future ones.
problem_spec.prediction_time: Immediately before publishing, after caption text, media type (video/image/carousel), and the planned posting day/hour are decided, but before the post goes live and before any engagement exists.
problem_spec.label_latency: Engagement accumulates over hours to a few days after publishing; for this offline/advisory use case label latency does not block iteration since labels are computed retrospectively from historical data, not needed in real time.

cost_ratio.false_positive: Operator revises a post that would have actually done fine — a few minutes of unnecessary rework.
cost_ratio.false_negative: Operator posts as-is and it underperforms — one missed opportunity to improve a single post, no other consequence.
cost_ratio.basis: This is an advisory-only, non-automated flag with no financial or safety consequence on either side; both error types cost a small amount of the operator's attention, not treated as asymmetric since neither is a guess dressed as a measurement.

floor.rationale: Modest bar chosen because it is genuinely uncertain whether pre-publish tabular/caption features carry enough signal on ~250-350 primary-platform posts to beat a coin flip by much. Set low enough to be clearable if real signal exists, high enough that matching the dummy still fails it.

baselines.name: coin-flip dummy
baselines.definition: Uniform random 0/1 prediction, ignoring all features. Non-degenerate here because the label is constructed to be ~50/50 by definition.

baselines.name: logistic regression on platform + content_type only
baselines.definition: Plain, untuned logistic regression using only the two cheapest categorical features, no caption/timing features, no hyperparameter tuning.

problem_spec.stopping_condition: If a tuned baseline-through-gradient-boosted-trees pass does not beat the coin-flip dummy by at least 5 percentage points of balanced accuracy, report a negative finding: the dataset is too small/noisy for this task in its current form, and revisit once real post volume roughly doubles per primary platform, rather than continuing to tune indefinitely.

constraints.latency_budget: not latency-sensitive; a single prediction can take seconds
constraints.cost_ceiling: no dedicated infra budget; must run on the existing VPS alongside the warehouse
